mainTopic: Creating a scent on יום טוב, the גדי מקולס, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's leniencies, including the rule of an unintended act (דבר שאינו מתכוין).
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling that spices may be placed on hot earthenware on יום טוב to make a nice smell. רבה forbids even that because it creates a new scent (מוליד ריחא), while רבא permits spices even on coals, like roasting meat on coals. A story follows: רב גביהא taught that קטורא is permitted, אמימר challenged it, and רב אשי explained that it means burning incense, which is permitted. The גמרא then discusses רבן גמליאל's leniency of a whole roasted goat (גדי מקולס) on פסח night, and why the חכמים objected to תודוס of Rome. A new משנה lists three things רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid: a cow with a strap between its horns, combing an animal, and grinding pepper in its mill. The גמרא explains that 'his cow' was really his neighbor's, called his because he did not protest. It then explains the three opinions on combing and brushing as a dispute about an unintended act (דבר שאינו מתכוין). It ends with רב נחמן ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, who permits an unintended act.

steps.title: Spices on hot earthenware are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier ruling: putting spices on a hot piece of earthenware on יום טוב is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But placing them on a hot piece of earthenware is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling that started just before this point. Spices may be placed on a hot piece of earthenware (חרס) on יום טוב to give off a smell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling before this was concerned with spices put right on the coals. A hot piece of earthenware has no burning coals, so there is no worry of putting out a fire or lighting one, and it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece of earthenware (here, a hot shard)

phrases.english: On a piece of earthenware — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence before it, about sprinkling spices to make a nice smell.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל גַּבֵּי חֶרֶס — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun before this section (spices on coals versus on earthenware).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices on a hot earthenware shard on יום טוב are permitted.

steps.title: רבה forbids even earthenware because it creates a scent
steps.stepSummary: רבה says putting spices on earthenware is also forbidden, because it creates a new smell (מוליד ריחא).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: on earthenware it is also forbidden, because he is creating a scent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה disagrees with the ruling we just saw. He forbids spices even on hot earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is not worried about fire here. His problem is that the spices make the earthenware give off a smell it never had. Creating something new like this (מוליד) is not allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Creating (literally, 'giving birth to') a new scent

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a whole new kind of problem, creating a new smell, alongside the fire worries. The rest of the passage builds on it.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
On earthenware it is also forbidden,
because he is producing a scent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה אָמַר: עַל גַּבֵּי חֶרֶס נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 1 and forbids the earthenware case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices on hot earthenware are forbidden because they create a new scent.

steps.title: A parallel ruling about perfume on silk clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both forbid turning a cup of perfume over onto silk clothing on יום טוב, for the same reason: it creates a scent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה and רב יוסף both said: turning a cup over onto silk clothes on יום טוב is forbidden. What is the reason? Because he is creating a scent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling that uses the same reason as רבה. It shows that רבה's idea of creating a scent shows up elsewhere too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring perfume onto silk makes the cloth smell in a way it did not before. Since this is forbidden for the same reason, it supports רבה's view on the earthenware case.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both said:

phrases.aramaic: סַחוֹפֵי כָּסָא אַשִּׁירָאֵי בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Overturning a cup onto silk garments on a Festival is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The cup has perfume in it, so turning it over leaves the smell on the silk.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because he is producing a scent.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 2 with a ruling based on the same reason.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's rule that creating a new scent is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The joint ruling of רבה and רב יוסף about perfume on silk clothes.

steps.title: Why is pressing fragrant wood allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if creating a scent is forbidden, why may one press or snip fragrant wood and smell it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from: he may press it and smell it, and snip it and smell it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea of מוליד ריחא. There is a known teaching that lets a person press or snip a piece of fragrant wood to smell it, and that also seems to make a smell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing or snipping fragrant wood releases more smell, so it seems to 'create' a scent. If that is allowed, why should perfume on silk, or spices on earthenware, be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? How is this case different?
He rubs or presses it between his fingers
He snips or breaks off a piece of it

phrases.english: And how is it different from 'he presses it and smells it'
phrases.notes: This quotes an earlier teaching about a piece of fragrant wood.

phrases.english: and 'he snips it and smells it'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִמּוֹלְלוֹ וּמֵרִיחַ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle of מוליד ריחא used in Steps 2–3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that making a scent on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pressing or snipping fragrant wood also makes smell, yet it is permitted, so making a smell should not be a problem.

steps.title: Adding to a scent versus creating a new one
steps.stepSummary: With the wood, the smell is already there and is only made stronger. With the perfume, a brand-new smell is created in the cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the scent exists anyway, and he is only adding to the scent. Here, he is creating a new scent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by telling the two cases apart. Making an existing smell stronger is fine, but giving a smell to something that had none is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fragrant wood already smells, and pressing it only increases the smell (אוסופי). The silk had no smell at all, so the perfume gives it a new one (אולודי). Only the second counts as creating something new.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the case of the wood)
Here (in our case of the perfume)

steps.whatToRemember: Strengthening a smell that already exists is permitted. Giving a new smell to something that had none (מוליד ריחא) is forbidden on יום טוב, according to רבה and רב יוסף.

phrases.english: There, the scent is there in any case,
and he is only adding to the scent.
Here, he is creating a scent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — רֵיחָא מִיהָא אִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any act that produces smell, including pressing fragrant wood, is the same as creating a scent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only giving a new smell to something without smell is forbidden. Strengthening a smell that is already there is allowed.

steps.title: רבא permits spices even on coals
steps.stepSummary: רבא says spices may be put even directly on coals, just as meat may be roasted on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: on a coal it is also permitted, just like meat on coals.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third, more lenient view. Even putting spices right onto burning coals is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about coals was that you put out part of the fire. רבא compares it to roasting meat on coals, which is clearly allowed on יום טוב even though it touches the coals in the same way.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה (with a ה) and רבא (with an א) are two different אמוראים. Here רבה forbids even earthenware, while רבא permits even coals.

phrases.english: Rava said:
On a coal it is also permitted,
just as with meat on coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: עַל גַּבֵּי גַּחֶלֶת נָמֵי מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the coal-versus-earthenware ruling and gives the most lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices may be placed even directly on coals on יום טוב, like roasting meat on coals.

steps.title: רב גביהא teaches that קטורא is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהא of בי כתיל taught publicly at the ריש גלותא's house that קטורא is permitted on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהא from בי כתיל taught at the entrance of the ריש גלותא's house: קטורא is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רב גביהא gave a short public ruling that קטורא is permitted, without explaining what he meant, and this sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קטורא can mean two things: tying knots or burning incense. Because he did not say which one, the next step will ask what he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Babylonia
An unclear word: tying knots, or burning incense

phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Katil taught
at the entrance to the house of the Exilarch:
Ketura is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב גְּבִיהָא מִבֵּי כְתִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about a related ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קטורא is permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: אמימר: either meaning should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אמימר asks what קטורא means. If it means tying knots by hand, that is skilled work. If it means burning incense, it puts out coals. Either way it should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said to him: What is קטורא? If it is tying by hand, that is a craftsman's work. And if it is for making smoke, it is forbidden, because he is putting out fire!
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר challenges רב גביהא's ruling. He shows that both possible meanings of קטורא seem to be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying fancy knots is skilled craftsman's work (מעשה אומן), which is not allowed on יום טוב. Sprinkling incense on coals partly puts them out (מכבה). So whichever way you read it, the ruling looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of a skilled craftsman
To make smoke, to burn incense

phrases.english: Ameimar said to him:
What is 'ketura'?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קִטּוּרָא בִּידֵי — מַעֲשֵׂה אוּמָּן הוּא,
phrases.english: If it is tying by hand, that is a craftsman's work,
phrases.notes: Here 'ketura' is read as tying knots, from the Aramaic word for tying (קטר).

phrases.english: and if it means to make smoke, it is forbidden,
because he is extinguishing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַמֵּימָר: מַאי קִטּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 7 by testing both possible meanings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גביהא's ruling that קטורא is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both meanings are forbidden. Tying knots is a craftsman's work, and burning incense puts out coals.

steps.title: רב אשי: it means incense, like meat on coals
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that קטורא really means burning incense, and that is permitted just like roasting meat on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Really it means making smoke, and it is just like meat on coals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רב גביהא's ruling. He says it means burning incense, and he uses the same comparison רבא used earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר's worry was that the coals get partly put out. רב אשי answers that roasting meat on coals has the same effect and is still allowed, so incense on coals is allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (I keep my first meaning)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי, like רבא, holds that putting spices or incense on coals on יום טוב is permitted, comparing it to roasting meat on coals.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
Actually, it means to make smoke,
just as with meat on coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לְעוֹלָם לְעַשֵּׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אמימר's challenge in Step 8 using רבא's comparison from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing one meaning and defending it with a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning incense on coals is forbidden because it puts out the coals.
steps.terutzMaskana: קטורא means burning incense, which is permitted just like roasting meat on coals.

steps.title: A second version of Ameimar's challenge
steps.stepSummary: In another version, אמימר asks about קטורא. Tying knots by hand is skilled work, and burning incense is forbidden because it creates a new smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell the story differently. אמימר asked: What does 'קטורא' mean? If it means tying knots by hand, that is a craftsman's work. If it means burning incense, that is forbidden because it creates a new smell!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way the story was told. In this version אמימר attacks the incense ruling for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 8), burning incense was a problem because it puts out coals. Here the problem is מוליד ריחא, creating a new smell. That links back to the perfume case in step 5, where creating a brand-new smell was the issue.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: a second version of the same story
Creating a new smell, which is a problem on יום טוב
To burn incense and make smoke

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument added on top of step 8. It is the same conversation told a different way. The only thing that changes is why burning incense would be forbidden.

phrases.english: Some say:
Ameimar said to him:
What is "ketura"?
If it means tying knots by hand,
that is the work of a craftsman.
If it means burning incense,
it is forbidden, because he creates a new smell!

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי אמר ליה אמימר מאי קטורא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the challenge of step 8 with a different reason for forbidding incense
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גביהא's public teaching that קטורא is permitted on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both meanings of קטורא seem forbidden. Tying knots is skilled work, and burning incense creates a new smell (מוליד ריחא).

steps.title: רב אשי again permits incense like roasting meat
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says he taught this in the name of a great man (רבא): קטורא means burning incense, and it is permitted just like putting meat on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I told it to him, and I told it in the name of a great man. It really means burning incense, and it is just like meat on coals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers אמימר's challenge in this second version. He says the ruling came from him, quoting a great authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי keeps the meaning 'burning incense' and still permits it. He compares it to roasting meat on coals, which is allowed on יום טוב even though it also gives off smell. The 'great man' points back to רבא's ruling in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, meaning a major authority
Really / actually: the one meaning we keep
Just like: a comparison to a known case

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the bottom line is the same: burning incense on coals on יום טוב is permitted, just like roasting meat on coals.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said it to him,
and I said it to him in the name of a great man:
phrases.notes: The great man is רבא, whose ruling about spices on coals we saw a little earlier.

phrases.english: It really means burning incense,
and it is just like meat on coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי אנא אמריתה ניהליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second version of אמימר's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a permitted case (roasting meat on coals)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning incense creates a new smell and should be forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: It is permitted, just as roasting meat on coals is permitted

steps.title: תודוס of Rome and the whole roasted goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next case in the משנה, the גדי מקולס. It quotes a ברייתא: תודוס of Rome started a custom of eating a whole roasted goat on פסח night, and the חכמים said they would have put him in נידוי if not for his importance.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they make a whole roasted goat.' It was taught: רבי יוסי says, תודוס of Rome led the Jews of Rome to eat a whole roasted goat on the nights of פסח. The חכמים sent to him: If you were not תודוס, we would put you in נידוי, because you are feeding the Jewish people קדשים outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, the גדי מקולס. It brings a ברייתא with a story about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goat roasted whole looks like a קרבן פסח. The חכמים were upset that תודוס made a custom that looked like eating קדשים outside the בית המקדש. They held back from punishing him only because of who he was.

keyTerms.meaning: A young goat roasted whole, the way the קרבן פסח was roasted
It was taught in a ברייתא
Holy offerings eaten outside the place they may be eaten

phrases.english: "And they make a whole roasted goat."
It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Todos, a man of Rome,
led the people of Rome
to eat a whole roasted goat
on the nights of Pesach.
They sent to him:
Were you not Todos,
we would decree a ban upon you,
for you are feeding the Jewish people
holy offerings outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: ועושין גדי מקולס תניא רבי יוסי אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the incense discussion to the next leniency in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a custom of eating a whole roasted goat on פסח night outside the בית המקדש is strongly frowned upon, because it looks like eating קדשים outside.

steps.title: Could it really be holy offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can call the goats קדשים, when they were obviously never consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy offerings? Can that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the ברייתא's wording. This sets up the correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary goats bought and roasted at home are not קדשים at all. So the words 'קדשים בחוץ' cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (meaning: surely not)

phrases.english: Holy offerings? Can that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קדשים סלקא דעתך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'קדשים בחוץ' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These goats were never consecrated, so calling them קדשים makes no sense.

steps.title: Read it as similar to holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading: he was feeding them something that looks like קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: something like holy offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was never that the meat was holy. The problem was that a whole roasted goat on פסח night looks just like a קרבן פסח, and people could mistake it for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא's correction of a wording

steps.whatToRemember: The concern with גדי מקולס is that it looks like a קרבן פסח, not that it actually is one.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
something like holy offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אימא כעין קדשים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by correcting the reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא literally means real קדשים
steps.terutzMaskana: It means food that looks like קדשים

steps.title: New משנה: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's three leniencies
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists three things רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid. The first is a cow going out with a strap between its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are three things that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid. His cow would go out with a strap between its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It opens a list of three disputes, and the first is about a cow wearing a strap between its horns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets up a list of three cases where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is lenient and the חכמים are strict. The first case is about letting his cow go out with a strap between its horns.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
The תנא who is lenient in these three cases

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Three things
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya permits
and the Rabbis forbid:
His cow would go out
with a strap between its horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: שלשה דברים רבי אלעזר בן עזריה מתיר וחכמים אוסרים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after finishing the discussion of רבן גמליאל's leniencies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits his cow to go out with a strap between its horns, and the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: The second and third leniencies: combing an animal and grinding pepper
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the list of things רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits: combing an animal on יום טוב, and grinding pepper in its own pepper mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may comb an animal on יום טוב. And one may grind peppers in their own mill.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing the list of three things that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid. Here are items two and three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Item two is combing an animal with a fine comb to clean its hair, which the חכמים worry could wound it. Item three is grinding pepper in a real pepper mill on יום טוב, even though that looks like ordinary weekday work.

keyTerms.meaning: Combing an animal with a fine-toothed comb to remove dirt and ticks

phrases.english: And one may comb the animal on יום טוב.
phrases.notes: This is still part of the list from Step 15, so it is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.

phrases.english: And one may grind the peppers
in their own mill.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-item list opened in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, one may comb an animal and grind pepper in its own mill on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and the חכמים on combing versus brushing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids fine combing because it wounds the animal but allows brushing. The חכמים forbid both combing and brushing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One may not comb an animal on יום טוב, because it makes a wound, but one may brush it. And the חכמים say: One may not comb, and one may not even brush.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings two more opinions about cleaning an animal's hair on יום טוב. So we now have three levels of strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says fine combing surely makes a wound, so it is forbidden, but brushing with a blunter comb is fine. The חכמים are the strictest and forbid even brushing. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from Step 16 is the most lenient and allows combing.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound, a bruise that breaks the skin or draws blood
Brushing an animal with a large-toothed comb

steps.confusionAlert: There are three opinions here, not two. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows combing, רבי יהודה allows only brushing, and the חכמים forbid both.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not comb the animal on יום טוב,
because it makes a wound,
but one may brush.
And the Sages say:
One may not comb, and not even brush.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more opinions on the combing case from Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: combing is forbidden since it wounds, brushing is allowed. חכמים: both combing and brushing are forbidden.

steps.title: Did רבי אלעזר בן עזריה really own just one cow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה speaks of 'his cow', when רב taught that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה tithed thirteen thousand calves from his herds every year.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Is that to say that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה had only one cow? But didn't רב say, and some say רב יהודה said in the name of רב: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would tithe thirteen thousand calves from his herds every single year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case of the משנה, 'his cow goes out with a strap' (Step 15), and challenges it. It does not fit what we know about how rich he was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה talks as if he had one cow. But רב says he gave thirteen thousand calves a year as מעשר בהמה, which is one out of every ten. So he had huge herds, and talking about 'his cow' sounds strange.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a surprising implication)
And some say (a second version of who said it)
Was tithing (separating one out of ten animals)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is that to say that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
phrases.notes: This is about the first item of the משנה from Step 15, the cow with the strap between its horns.

phrases.english: had only one cow?
But didn't Rav say,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
thirteen thousand calves

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְעַשַּׂר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya would tithe
from his herds each and every year.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה חֲדָא פָּרָה הַוְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion by going back to the first case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording 'his cow' (פרתו) for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man who tithed 13,000 calves a year owned enormous herds, so it makes no sense to speak of 'his cow' as if he had one.

steps.title: The cow was his neighbor's, called by his name
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that the cow belonged to his neighbor. Because he did not protest her conduct, the cow was called by his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The cow was not his. It was his neighbor's, and because he did not protest to her, it was called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 18 with a ברייתא. 'His cow' does not mean he owned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor let her cow go out with the strap, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה did not tell her not to. Since he could have protested and didn't, the act is blamed on him, and the cow is called 'his'. This also takes care of the one-cow problem.
steps.whatToRemember: 'His cow' was really his neighbor's. It was called his because he did not protest, which shows that someone who could protest and stays quiet shares the blame.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a big idea: a person who can stop a wrong and does not is held responsible as if he did it himself.

phrases.english: It was taught:
It was not his,
rather, it was his neighbor's,
and because he did not protest to her,
it was called by his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: לֹא שֶׁלּוֹ הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording: 'his cow' means a cow blamed on him, not a cow he owned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means a cow that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה owned, as if he had just one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cow belonged to his neighbor, and it is called his because he failed to protest.

steps.title: Defining combing and brushing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about combing and brings a ברייתא that defines the two terms: combing uses small teeth and wounds, brushing uses large teeth and does not wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may comb the animal on יום טוב.' The רבנן taught: What is combing and what is brushing? Combing is with small teeth and makes a wound. Brushing is with large teeth and does not make a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case of the משנה, combing an animal. It brings a ברייתא to explain the two words used in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרוד uses a comb with small, thin teeth, which do cut into the skin. קרצוף uses a comb with large, blunt teeth, which do not. This explains why רבי יהודה in Step 17 forbids one and allows the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Combing with a fine, small-toothed comb

steps.whatToRemember: קרוד uses small teeth and wounds. קרצוף uses large teeth and does not wound.

phrases.english: And one may comb the animal on יום טוב.
The Rabbis taught:
What is combing and what is brushing?
Combing: small ones, and they make a wound,
phrases.notes: 'Small ones' means the teeth of the comb.

phrases.english: brushing: large ones, and they do not make a wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ קֵרוּד וְאֵיזֶהוּ קִרְצוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the cow case, the גמרא moves to the second case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרוד is done with a small-toothed comb and wounds; קרצוף is done with a large-toothed comb and does not wound.

steps.title: Three opinions, starting with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there are three opinions here. It explains that רבי יהודה forbids an unintended act, so he forbids combing, which wounds, but permits brushing, which does not. He does not forbid brushing as a safeguard for combing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three opinions on this. רבי יהודה holds that an act done without intending the forbidden result is still forbidden. But he separates the two cases. Combing uses small teeth and causes a wound, so it is forbidden. Brushing uses large teeth and does not cause a wound, so it is allowed. He does not forbid brushing out of worry about combing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins laying out the reasoning behind the three opinions in the משנה, starting with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the person only wants to clean the animal, רבי יהודה holds that a forbidden result he did not intend still makes the act forbidden. Combing with small teeth wounds the animal, so it is forbidden. Brushing with large teeth does not wound, and he does not add a גזירה against it.

keyTerms.meaning: An act where the forbidden result is not what the person intends
We make a rabbinic decree, a protective rule
Because of, out of concern for

phrases.english: And there are three disputes in this matter.
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
An unintended act is forbidden.
However: combing uses small teeth,
and they make a wound.
Brushing uses large teeth,
and they do not make a wound.
And we do not decree against brushing because of combing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחְלוֹקוֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definitions from step 20 (small teeth wound, large teeth do not) to explain רבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: an unintended act is forbidden, so combing is forbidden. Brushing is permitted, with no גזירה.

steps.title: The view of the חכמים and of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה that an unintended act is forbidden, but they also forbid brushing because of combing. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה follows רבי שמעון, who permits an unintended act, so he allows both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים also hold like רבי יהודה that an unintended act is forbidden. But they do make a decree against brushing because of combing. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds like רבי שמעון, who said an unintended act is permitted, so both combing and brushing are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the three opinions by explaining the חכמים and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים share רבי יהודה's basic principle. They differ only by adding a גזירה: brushing might be confused with combing, so they forbid it too. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה disagrees with the basic principle itself, so for him nothing here is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, meaning the חכמים in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים and רבי יהודה agree on the basic rule about unintended acts. Their only argument is whether to add a protective decree against brushing.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis also hold like Rabbi Yehuda,
that an unintended act is forbidden,
but we do decree against brushing because of combing.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה סָבַר לַהּ
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya holds
like Rabbi Shimon, who said:
An unintended act is permitted,
so both combing and brushing are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי נָמֵי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-opinion breakdown begun in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים forbid both because of a גזירה. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, following רבי שמעון, permits both.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting שמואל according to one version, rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, because רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן, who said it in the name of שמואל. Some say רב נחמן said it on his own. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final ruling on the question of unintended acts: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is support: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in our משנה holds the same view as רבי שמעון. The גמרא also records two versions of who first said this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it this way

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling that an unintended act is permitted, following רבי שמעון, is a basic rule that applies far beyond combing animals.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן לְחוֹדֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Nachman said it himself:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מוֹדֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: since Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the three views are explained, a practical ruling is given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון that an unintended act is permitted, supported by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבא asks why not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: by the same logic, you could rule like רבי יהודה, since the חכמים agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Let the master say instead that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, since the חכמים agree with him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reason רב נחמן gave for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is 'someone in the משנה agrees,' that works even better for רבי יהודה. The חכמים, a majority, agree with him that an unintended act is forbidden. So the reason seems to point the other way.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Then let the master say,
that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
since the Sages agree with him!
phrases.notes: They agree with him on the basic rule, even though they add the decree against brushing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: וְלֵימָא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reason that the agreement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה decides the הלכה for רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If agreement is the deciding factor, רבי יהודה has stronger support, since the חכמים agree with his basic principle.

steps.title: רב נחמן: I hold like רבי שמעון anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he holds like רבי שמעון on his own reasoning. The agreement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is only an extra support, not the main reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I myself hold like רבי שמעון. And beyond that, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling by explaining that the agreement was never his main reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's challenge assumed that agreement decides the הלכה. רב נחמן explains that his ruling comes from his own view that רבי שמעון is right. The support of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is only added backing, so the agreement of the חכמים with רבי יהודה does not change anything.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold, it is my view

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: an unintended act (דבר שאינו מתכוין) is permitted. רב נחמן rules this way from his own reasoning, and the support of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is only extra backing.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I hold like Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד שֶׁהֲרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מוֹדֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: and furthermore, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the reason: the agreement was extra support, not the main basis
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling for רבי שמעון rested only on the agreement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן holds like רבי שמעון on his own. The agreement only adds support.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון that an unintended act is permitted.
